assertion: Americans traveling this holiday season are facing some of the highest airfares in a decade due to the surge in jet fuel prices earlier this year stemming from the Iran war.
inaccuracy: The claim presents the decade-high as established; it rests on Hopper's own fare index, not a government series, and the fuel surge was not only 'earlier this year' (fuel rose again to $4.30-$4.53 in September).
independent_value: Hopper $402/$452 (+31%/+23%); BLS Sept airline fares +22.4% y/y; AP: airfares +23% y/y in August
searched: CPI airline fares October 2026 year over year BLS

assertion: rebounded to $4.90 a gallon in late October, according to data from the Argus U.S. Jet Fuel Index
reason: Argus data is paywalled; AP reported $4.53 on Sept 17 and $4.30 on Sept 26; airlines.org showed only $3.47 on Nov 23. $4.90 in late October is plausible but no source found.
